title: Composition 32
standfirst: Thirty-two small vistas on one canvas, each dragged out of a single pure colour. Painted on 19 July 2026, between PixelArcade and the //Strips.

blocks.text: Thirty-two leaves
Composition 32 is one canvas, 1200 by 600 mm, divided into thirty-two squares. Four rows of eight. Each square holds a small vista of its own.
The square
Each square is 150 mm. The pixel of the piece.

The square and the grid came out of **[FROGDNA](/c/frogdna)** and **[PixelArcade](/c/pixelarcade)**, where the pixel was the unit of everything. FROGDNA sampled eighty-eight pixels from eighty-eight Pepes. PixelArcade winnowed each arcade game down to its essential palette.
Here each square starts from a pure colour sourced from the PixelArcade series.
Then the colour is dragged.
The drag
The technique comes from **[Two Burdens](/c/two-burdens)** (2024). Paint is dragged across the surface, Richter-like, and the combinations and permutations mix as the paint hits the canvas.
Nothing is fully planned. The colours meet in the drag and settle where they settle. A pure colour goes in. A place comes out.
1976 ... Gerhard Richter

FROGDNA was in conversation with Richter's Colour Charts of 1966. Composition 32 talks to the other Richter. In 1976 he began small abstract paintings that let him do what he had never let himself do... put something down at random. Then he found it never can be random.
The drag is chance with a hand on it.
11th century ... the album leaf

In China, small paintings were mounted as the leaves of an album, turned one at a time and then put away. In the eleventh century the official and painter Song Di set out eight scenes of the Xiao and Xiang rivers. The Eight Views became one of the most painted themes in East Asia, carried to Korea and Japan.

Few of the painters who took up the Eight Views had ever seen the place. They painted its mood instead... dim light, mist, evening snow. Japanese painters went on to make sets of their own, like the Eight Views of Ōmi.
The thirty-two vistas here work the same way. Places that may echo familiarity, yet their form lies just out of grasp.
An album asks you to look at one leaf, then the next. Composition 32 lays all thirty-two out at once, and the eye still reads them one by one.
Turned on its end
Hung upright, the drag lies down. Streaks become horizons, and the squares read as shore, sea and sky.
Composition
The title borrows a heavy word. Kandinsky gave the name Composition to only ten paintings, made between 1910 and 1939, and counted them his most important. He kept them apart from his improvisations.
Composition 32 sits in between. Thirty-two improvised drags, held in one composed grid.
2026 ... the pivot
Composition 32 was painted on 19 July 2026. Going back to Two Burdens didn't feel right, and the //Strips hadn't arrived yet. It was a time to experiment and reorientate.
That time made the space for the **[//Strips](/c/strip-paintings)** to arrive.
2026 ... exhibition
Composition 32 has been exhibited at The Line in Hastings, New Zealand.
The 1/1 painting has been collected by Shaun Peterson.
Availability
The painting has been collected, at NZD 1,000 including GST.
